title: The Frost That Stayed

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The week goes out as it came in. The trough skins over, the yard calls it weather, and the hand goes up an inch and comes down.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the drying racks in Low Kiln, told at the going of a working week

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and seventy-six to two hundred and seventy-eight days, six months and ninety-six to six months and ninety-eight days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing — the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the body inventoried as a wound of crust, gap, frozen thread, cold and afterdrop in the order they arrive; the frost-shinned trough read as a vessel with a skin laid over it; the held interval and the empty interval kept as objects on the sixth place and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a doctrine or a rule — with no present-tense Chicago break and no tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no sixth hearing, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question (the five askings and the one further shaping stand as they stood), no tenth record-first hand, no eighth of the green or the shape, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause, no sign, lesson, mending or payer made of the first firing of Frost, no bond changed hands, no private record opened, read or copied, no figure given for the covered grain, and no ending. Frost 10 (Day 279), the month's first Account-day and market, stands one morning beyond the close and is not brought into a day that has not earned it.

scenes.title: The Seventh Morning
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and the first \daymark{276}{...}: Day 276, Frost 7, Seventhday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first light of the working week's last third. Open in the small hours with the hand laid down against the fold on the one hundred and twenty-sixth answer as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. No recap of Chapter 74; the reader has just read it. Carry 275 to 276 exact, six months and ninety-six days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-six days, its payer unnamed (T088). Body inventory in the old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone past the point where a child would eat it, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knows a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and wants the crust lifted two inches. Both true, the second louder in a body two hundred and seventy-six days old, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Three counts in three places: the fire's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, the river's water over water at the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot. Agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands (T061/T082); the heard bell's four, four and a gap stays in the square beside the told bell of the Long Night and is not folded in (T078). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells the coals the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives no instruction at any hour to the basket (T058/T079, T100). The widow's mark hangs where it hangs, touched once before the kiln on Frost 2 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, morning, hearth, afternoon, dusk or going of the light because none is an opening; the first firing of Frost is not looked at again as sign, lesson, mending or payment, four openings are four and not a rule, and the next stands in a later month's first firing, far off (T058/T079). Frost 7 comes on its own light and was not brought into Day 275; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Seventhday and Frost 10 stands three mornings ahead, unbrought. The hand answers one hundred and twenty-seven: up an inch for the small intake of the river's own note, carried across the little silence after one of the breaths counted in the room whose floor does not touch, and down on the next low note, borrowing no house count and supplying no fifth (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Instruction to the Pot
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 276, no new dated heading: afternoon thinning into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the yard well and bare dark trough, the drying racks and the cool stone at the rack end, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the loaf shelf, the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending, the way heat goes out of a pot set off the coals; heat draws back out of the fold and goes to sit behind the pot. One leathery crust two inches off, gap unnamed, no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). Sella carries the basket at the half-pace from every open slate and goes wide around the seven places with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the finer grey hairline called the thaw beside it, unswept both; the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates; the round ring where the shallow clay pan stood with no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word; the bare dark trough beside the yard well with its water called weather; the field's empty place out on the worked strips; and the returning-line place where the hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out. Seven are seven and not an account, because an account wants a payer standing under it and none stands; the missing hand is carried and not named, not paid and not joined to the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust or the dressed grain (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). The dressed grain is turned once beneath the wool for damp with a lighter touch and given no figure, the arithmetic to come not knowing what it cost (T077). Smoke's third arithmetic stays unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box and the figure read is still not the figure paid (T015/T041/T047). Garl is kept in objects and not in a story, his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-six days: the salt-stiff coat with the left-shoulder crease, the hollow wheel-seat no one may fill, the proverb said to the pot and the fire and never to a person, the debt against a firing of tiles neither paid nor settled nor done with and worse for being uncalled. No collector came up the clay road on Frost 7 and none went down it (T009/T013/T092). Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the very lip of the kindling sill beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, draws the breath he does not spend and brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan before stopping there with no figure and no name — a remembered ninth stopping and no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, still ungiven; his stroke goes over the shallow bright patch without the half-check, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is, the warm stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot (T036/T076, T006). Jorra parts meal-fine grey slate dust from clean forearms, speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person, withholds the full note he knows three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it, gives the men who went low into the back room before first grey no name, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both; burned slate stays at four from Slate Row, shut-room tellings at two, three pot sayings with the premature Smoke 14 note on its own place and no fourth likeness made a cause, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness and no row named, he's not Vail sealed and the promise of the boy's name ungiven (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101, T064). A woman with a pot asks what the keeping and storing will take now the grain is under wool and the visits coming and is sent to the pot and the weather with nothing priced, refused or entered. The hand answers one hundred and twenty-eight: takes the hold of one of the counted breaths and comes down on the river's note while that count is still letting go, leaving the letting-go and the little silence after it whole and outside the holding (T061/T082).

scenes.title: What the Sun Did Not Take
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark{277}{...}: Day 277, Frost 8, Eighthday, Y.H. 813, the small hours under the Vail roof, out onto the Clay Yard into the morning and past noon. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 8 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 276; there is no market, Cross or bell on an Eighthday; Frost 10 stands two mornings ahead and is not brought early. Carry 276 to 277 exact, six months and ninety-seven days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-seven days, its payer unnamed (T088). First smells as before: hot clay cooled under tallow, wet wool, the sour breath of the unswept corner called the thaw; rime lies heavier on the step; the kiln answers in fours with its gap, not a bell; the river keeps water over water; the boards keep four nails, four and a knot. Sella's grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, The house will keep it, half-pace from every open slate, pot handle two inches out, fold put right without a look at his face, thread left frozen, finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and the widow's mark untouched at a morning, a hearth and a rack, because none is an opening (T058/T079, T100). The dressed grain is turned beneath the wool for damp and given no figure; Smoke's third arithmetic stays behind and unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box and the figure read is still not the figure paid (T077, T015/T041/T047). THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, ADVANCED AND NOT PAID: on Frost 8 the white fronds the frost wrote on the well lip do not go when the sun is up, as they went on Frost 4, and the yard still calls it weather, and the frost stays past noon into the afternoon; the boy keeps the stayed frost on a place of its own beside the white thing kept from Frost 4 and the wrong wind's sweet edge of lead glaze from Frost 2, a direction arrived nowhere, and does not lay any two together, for a joining would want a payer and none stands. It is a real change in the day's work and the yard's body — the well rope stiffens, the trough takes a skin, the coals are banked an hour earlier — and it is entered nowhere, made into no sign, no lesson, no cause and no account, and is not paid by the nearness of Frost 10 (T083/T085 advanced, not paid; T061/T082). The finding that a house keeps by its not-doings stays a finding with no payer on a place of its own, not laid across the stayed frost, the boy's own kept gaps or the house's omissions with a finger between (T061/T082). A wrong wind off High Kiln is a direction arrived nowhere and no fourth likeness is made a cause (T064). The hand answers one hundred and twenty-nine: holds two intakes from the room whose floor does not touch apart with a finger between, the letting-go between them left where it was, and comes down on the river's next low note, neither intake made to agree with the fire's missing fifth (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Count in the Sleeve
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 277, no new dated heading: afternoon at the yard well, the bare trough now skinned at the edges and the drying racks, the flagstones and the wheel-shed edge, into the small hours at the bed and the towel. Afternoon thins without ending. One crust two inches off with its unnamed gap and no third; thread frozen; cold at cheek, temple and wrist; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). The stayed frost is called weather by everybody at the well and by nobody who has to pay for it, and no figure is put on it (T083/T085). Ilva is glimpsed once at the yard well drawing water with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and the finer grey rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb, which she does not scrub out. Asked what the month's firings have taken, her hand goes toward her sleeve and stays there; the short strip of notched birch is not taken out, read, asked about, taken a figure from or joined to the charcoal under the shelf, the cord, the knots, the pages, the tins, the missing hand or the pale line. Her eyes go to the asker and her mouth answers the question put and not the one behind it: Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account. She goes on with her water and nobody turns twice. The boy files no tenth record-first hand; the ninth stays on its own place with a finger between it and the eighth, the count stays in wood where no slate can take a figure off it, and she does not know she was read (T080 held at nine, not paid). The shallow bright patch on the flagstones is kept as it has been since Seed 22 and the broom stroke goes over it without the half-check, the stones still keeping the place where it stopped; the loft scrape on its own place and the carried man's pale line on another are not joined to it (T036/T076). Jorra's forearms carry meal-fine grey dust and he asks no question that would join them to a cause; the back room keeps its finger's width of open and its sound of low voices and gets no name from the house; the burned-slate word is a direction over the boards told four times and not a fifth telling, the two tellings of the counting room shut in the war stay at two and have not become three, and the three sayings about a pot keep the premature Smoke 14 note on its own place with no fourth likeness made a cause (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). No sixth asking comes over the boards and the silence is a keeping and not a sixth witness (T101). The hand answers one hundred and thirty: takes the small intake of one counted breath and the hold of the next and bridges them over the river's low note, the bridge kept as an object on the sixth place and no house count borrowed for it (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Skinned Trough
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark{278}{...}: Day 278, Frost 9, Ninthday, Y.H. 813, the small hours into the morning under the Vail roof and out onto the Clay Yard and the rack end. New day, new date, no recap. Frost 9 comes on its own morning, earned by that light, and was not brought into Day 277; there is no market, Cross or bell on a Ninthday; Frost 10 stands one morning ahead and is not brought early, and no figure from the reading reaches this day. Carry 277 to 278 exact, six months and ninety-eight days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and seventy-eight days, its payer unnamed (T088). First sounds and smells as before, with rime on the step heavier than on the two mornings gone and the river low over lower under the finger's-width door. Sella's grammar holds exactly: fire before basket, instruction to the fire, the wool, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, The house will keep it, half-pace from every open slate, pot handle two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, fold put right without a look at his face, thread left frozen, finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, and the widow's mark untouched at a morning, a hearth, a rack and a basket, because none is an opening (T058/T079, T100). The trough beside the yard well has skinned over in the two days of stayed frost, and Sella breaks the skin with the back of the broken pot she turns the coals with, lifts the plate of ice, sets it where it will not be trodden and draws what the yard calls weather, giving nobody a figure and telling the weather where to stand; the boy reads a vessel with a skin laid over it and keeps the broken plate on a place of its own beside the stayed frost and the white fronds of Frost 4, not joined to the two gaps above the shelf, the fold's one crust and its empty place or the field's empty place, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T083/T085 advanced, T009/T013/T092, T060/T086). The dressed grain is turned beneath the wool a second time that morning because the stone it lies on has gone cold, and given no figure; Smoke's third arithmetic stays unread up the clay road in Berr's locked box and the figure read is still not the figure paid, with no signature on the space between (T077, T015/T041/T047). The first firing of Frost is not looked at again as a sign, lesson, mending or payment, and the household's refusal to make a doctrine of four months' openings is kept as a finding with no payer, not laid across the house's not-doings or his own kept gaps, for a joining would want a payer and none stands (T058/T079, T061/T082). Garl is kept by objects, his name unspoken two hundred and seventy-eight days, the uncalled tile debt worse for being uncalled, and no collector up or down the clay road on Frost 7, 8 or 9 (T009/T013/T092). The seven walked-around places are gone around with a look and a wide step and no number, the returning-line hand carried and not named (T098). Tarn keeps six and the seventh at the lip, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there as a remembered ninth stopping, Seed 16 breath unspent, chest tight, Ash in the knuckles, the warm stone cold in its loft pot and not tried, which is not forgiveness (T036/T076, T006). The boy's hand answers one hundred and thirty-one: stays past a count's letting-go and through the little silence, sets the held interval beside the empty interval with a finger between, and comes down on the river's note before its next low note, the early ending an object and not a freedom (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The File Left Open
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 278, Frost 9, afternoon into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed, the boards and the towel. Frost goes out without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming the months is set right or left wrong; no lesson is made of four months' openings and the next opening stands in the first firing of a later month, far off. Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back from the fold; one leathery brown-edged crust two inches off with its unnamed gap and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform (T061/T082). The stayed frost lies on the well lip past the going of the light and the yard calls it weather still, entered nowhere; the broken plate of ice stands where it was set (T083/T085). Sella carries him up at the going of the light at the half-pace from every open slate, sets him on the bed under the roof and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, moves her lips along a row standing with two gaps and gives neither gap a figure, glances once at the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and gives no instruction at any hour to the basket. In the small hours the file is turned out on the towel as instruments are turned out for a man who will never be called to use them, each thing laid in its own place with room between, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air. Six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among, five from four sources and the sixth, the small flat knock out of a woman as the men lifted her, filed where a thing out of a person must go and never with the things that came from vessels; no seventh stands in the empty place and none is invented to fill it. The heard bell's four, four and a gap stays in the square beside the told bell of the Long Night, not folded in and not a seventh (T078). The premature pot note lies on its own place apart from the three sayings, burned slate at four, shut-room tellings at two, row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, nine stoppings with no tenth, nine record-first hands with Ilva's ninth unread and no tenth, seventh green a colour and seventh shape a shape with no eighth; Smoke's third arithmetic sits locked in Berr's box up the clay road, the figure read is still not the figure paid, and the dressed grain lies covered and unfigured under wool at the rack end with two turnings given this morning and the arithmetic that will read over it tomorrow not knowing what it cost (T077, T015/T041/T047, T080, T101, T100, T065/T095). The hand answers one hundred and thirty-two: takes the small intake of the river's own note and the hold of one of the counted breaths, sets them side by side with a finger between, neither promoted into a reach, a hearing, a gift or a keeping, and comes down on the river's next low note. One hundred and thirty-two is filed on the sixth place beside one hundred and thirty-one, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, and he makes nothing of it and will not let it stand up as a gift, because a gift wants a taker and nobody under this roof has taken anything (T061/T082). The hand lays back against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. Two hundred and seventy-eight stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill or Grath; six months and ninety-eight days are told by nobody, and the fire's fifth is unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed (T071/T072, T088). Nothing has been opened, named, called, paid or ended on this Ninthday; the file lies open on the towel with every gap left gap, every tray parted from its neighbour and nothing that had moved. Frost 10 (Day 279), the month's first Account-day and market, stands one morning ahead and is not brought into a day that has not earned it; the hand goes forward into the reading and the boy's low inventory goes on with it.
